name: The Monday Morning Customer Portal Incident
businessImpact: $600 per minute in customer support and delayed transactions

phaseUpdates.1: At 8:42 AM, customers began reporting that the portal would not load. Several employees also report trouble reaching internal tools.
phaseUpdates.2: The incident team is collecting information. Reports are incomplete and the initial scope is not yet confirmed.
phaseUpdates.3: New reports show that email and the public status page are working, while the portal and one internal tool remain unreliable.
phaseUpdates.4: A recent configuration change is associated with the timing, but another affected department reports the same symptom from a different network.
phaseUpdates.5: A first recovery attempt improves access for some users but does not restore the portal for everyone. Verification is now required.
phaseUpdates.6: Leadership wants a concise status update: impact, current action, confidence, and next checkpoint.
phaseUpdates.7: The incident is ready for an after-action review. Compare what teams believed with what the evidence ultimately established.

evidence.title: User interview
evidence.description: A conversation with someone who experienced the incident firsthand.
evidence.content: One customer service employee cannot load the portal from the office network. They can reach email and the public status page. A coworker in another department reports the same portal symptom.

evidence.title: Service desk tickets
evidence.description: Recent internal reports grouped by symptom, time, and department.
evidence.content: Tickets come from Customer Service, Finance, and one remote employee. All mention portal timeouts. One ticket says, 'the entire network is down,' but the user also confirms email is working.

evidence.title: Monitoring information
evidence.description: Availability and latency signals for the portal and related services.
evidence.content: The portal health check is green from the monitoring location, but transaction latency is elevated. Authentication, email, and the status page are healthy.

evidence.title: Recent change record
evidence.description: A record of work completed shortly before the first report.
evidence.content: A configuration change affecting a shared gateway was completed at 8:31 AM. The change passed a limited check from one location. It is a credible lead, not proof of cause.

evidence.title: Application and gateway logs
evidence.description: Technical records showing requests, errors, and dependency behavior.
evidence.content: Requests from several networks reach the gateway but fail during a dependency call. The error pattern began after the configuration change and is absent from unaffected services.

timeline: 8:31 AM — Shared gateway configuration change completed.
8:42 AM — First customer portal report received.
8:47 AM — Internal reports begin arriving from multiple departments.
9:22 AM — Portal access improves but requires broader verification.
9:35 AM — Service restored and follow-up work begins.
rootCause: A gateway configuration change altered how the portal reached a shared dependency. The limited post-change check did not exercise the affected request path from multiple networks.
verification: Portal loads for a representative internal user
Customer simulation succeeds from another network
Authentication and dependent services remain healthy
Error and latency signals return to baseline
Users confirm the original business task works
learningObjectives: Separate user experience from technical diagnosis
Request evidence for a specific question
Revise a hypothesis when evidence changes
Use risk, rollback, and verification before declaring recovery
